label: FALSIFIED: system-skill-advisor/README.md:44 claims that an unreachable daemon makes the CLI answer from runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py and mark the response degraded, but no production process spawns that file — .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs and .skilled/bin/system-skill-advisor-launcher.cjs contain no python/skill_advisor/degraded token, and the only repo mentions are signature inputs (freshness.ts:105, system-skill-advisor.js:152 consumed at :355). Type: drift doc-vs-code. Introduced v4.0.0.0/v4.0.0.16. Verify: rg -n "python|skill_advisor|degraded" .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs .skilled/bin/system-skill-advisor-launcher.cjs then stop the daemon and call the CLI.

CONFIRMED: the ask-surface once guard is four different contracts, not one. Pi keys on the operator message (ask-surface-guard.ts:66, used at :107); OpenCode keys on the assistant messageId (ask-surface-guard.js:102); dsh keys on the turn number (dsh/ask-surface-guard.mjs:107); Claude keeps no marker of its own and defers to payload.stop_hook_active (claude/ask-surface-stop.cjs:92). The shared core offers exactly one mechanism (markTurn, ask-surface-core.cjs:180) and Claude would survive its removal untouched. Type: drift plus over-engineering; what breaks if the marker goes: Pi, OpenCode and dsh. Introduced v4.0.2.0.

Bug: the dsh ask-surface guard marks dsh:<sessionId>:<turn> (dsh/ask-surface-guard.mjs:107) and then calls agent.steer (:111), which by the adapter's own header comment makes the agent take one more step (module header, line 5) — a further step is a further turn number, so markTurn hands back a fresh key and the guard can steer again. Nothing compares the steered message provenance (source.kind 'repo-guards', line 81) against the turn being judged. The once-per-operator-turn contract is therefore absent on dsh, and the only test bounds itself to one turn number: tests/dsh-ask-surface-guard.test.mjs:36 says a second stop *in that turn* is not steered. Confidence medium-high because the turn numbering is inferred from the header comment. Introduced v4.0.2.0. Verify: emit two agent/turn-stopping events with turn 1 then turn 2 and the same prose menu and count agent.steer calls.

CONFIRMED: only one adapter test pins the once-per-operator-turn contract — pi/ask-surface-guard.test.ts:64 'sends one operator turn back once, however many agent loops end in the menu'. lib/ask-surface-core.test.mjs:62 pins markTurn only for the key it is handed. dsh (tests/dsh-ask-surface-guard.test.mjs:36) stops at one turn number. Claude (claude/ask-surface-stop.test.mjs:49) pins only that the guard respects stop_hook_active:true, so its once-per-operator-turn behaviour is a host contract the repo cannot test. Suite state at HEAD: node --test over claude plus lib plus dsh gives 31/31 pass. Type: verification gap.

CONFIRMED: no non-test caller of skill_advisor.py produces an operator-visible ranking. The live callers are create-skill-parent-auto.yaml:240 (--emit-routing-projection, a skill-creation routing projection), init-skill-graph.sh:86 (--health, diagnostics) and routing-accuracy/capture-local-native-divergence-ledger.mjs:154 (research harness); the plugin and freshness references (system-skill-advisor.js:152/355, freshness.ts:105) are cache-signature inputs that never spawn the file, and .github only comments on it (skill-advisor-stress.yml:8). Both flags those shell callers use exist (skill_advisor.py:5435 --emit-routing-projection, :5445 --health), so they are not broken — they are off the recommendation path. Consequence: the production surface of the script is a generator helper plus a health check, while README.md:44 still sells it as the runtime fallback scorer; the fix is the README line, not the script. Type: over-engineering plus drift. Introduced v4.0.0.0. Verify: rg -n "skill_advisor\.py" -g '!**/tests/**' -g '!**/*.test.*' -g '!**/dist/**' .opencode .skilled .github

The advisor status vocabulary carries a bare 'n' token where every sibling is a word: outageLabel 'absent'|'n'|'fail_open' in runtime/lib/render.ts and ADVISOR_HOOK_STATUS_VALUES ['ok','skipped','stale','n','fail_open'] in runtime/lib/metrics.ts. Looks like a redaction artifact rather than a designed state.

skill-advisor.cjs carries no 'degraded' token at all, so a daemon-down answer is distinguishable from a live one only through the brief's own status field — relevant to the UX question, not a separate finding.
